abstract: Production of cultivated meat demands a supply of cells that differentiate into muscle, even after extended proliferation. As primary bovine satellite cells (PrimSCs) lose proliferation and differentiation capacity over prolonged culture, immortalised cell lines are necessary for rapid commercialisation. Here, we report the first evidence of a transgene-free single knockout mRNA-hit-and-run-based strategy that yields immortalised bovine satellite cells (ImmSCs). We demonstrate targeted disruption of CDKN2A alone is sufficient to immortalise SCs from three cow breeds. ImmSCs maintained a 17h doubling time over 75 population doublings, while sustaining myogenic potential in 2D and 3D differentiation. Transcriptionally, ImmSCs evade senescence and continue to resemble young primary cells. Finally, we show that ImmSCs are non-tumorigenic and proliferate even with a 90% reduction in FGF-2, HGF, and T3. By combining immortalisation with regulatory compatibility, we demonstrate a simple and generalisable single-locus disruption strategy that minimizes batch variability and enables scalable production of cultivated meat.
